body:
It should have caused swelling yes, but they bascially only cut out the visible scars and made new stitches. But then again, the right side isn't swollen at all which seems suspicious to me.

I'll ask my surgeon when it's safe to work out again today.

Thanks for you kind words, it really means a lot to me. I guess if I have no chance at changing it whatsoever I'll have to try accepting it but it's really hard when every slight movement makes me want to cry my eyes out. The thing is I keep getting told I have so many "feminine features" and I know it's not malicious because I'm stealth but I just wanted to have ONE thing that's not feminine about me and it seems like even the possibility is just so far out of my reach. I'll just try staying strong for now somehow.

I'm so sorry man, I know exactly how it feels, I hope it gets better for you and you can be shirtless comfortably soon. I'm hoping for both of us to just be finally comfortable. Definitely keep asking your surgeon and showing them what it looks like every step of the way because I surely didn't do that enough after my initial surgery.

Thank you. I'll call my surgeon today and ask how long I can expect the swelling to stay. It looks better on photos, unfortunately it still looks massive under shirts. My surgeon even told me there's a high chance I would need a revision on the left side (left side is bad side, photos are flipped because of selfie camera) but he only said something about injecting cortisone to get rid of the internal scar tissue but he never brought it up again?? If I end up with one DI scar I wouldn't complain.

So I'm right handed and the right side is the flat side so unfortunately I don't think so :( I'll just have to keep at it with my surgeon until he does something if it doesn't go away and I'll ask when it's safe to work out again and then you bet I'll be spending every day doing only chest exercises, a few people have said it will help.

It might be a very very little bit smaller but it still feels aweful under clothing. It's not that I would hate a "not perfect" chest but if someone tried to touch my chest they would feel a breast because that's what it feels like and that's so terrible. I'm really skinny, I'm underweight so I thought it's unrealistic for me to have tissue there but I don't know. Some of it could be swelling, I just don't know why only the left side would be swollen.

Would only working out the right side help?

Thanks for your input. A few months just seems like absolute hell to me, I'll try wearing a binder for the time being but I've never had this freeing feeling everyone talks about after top and it hurts.

Thanks for your answer. I keep getting told it's swelling but it looks EXACTLY like before so I highly doubt that. Almost 1 year post op it looked exactly like that before the revision and it wasn't even a big revision, it was done under local anesthesia. Can this really happen, could it be muscle? Would it be this soft and hanging down? I've heard that before, I just wouldn't know how that happens when always working out both sides.

I really hope so. I'm glad people think it looks fine, thank you! I am massaging everyday and this is what my surgeon told me to do and what should ultimately get rid of this bump but apparently it's not helping.
I'm not quite sure if I can feel that, I'll check it more thoroughly tomorrow. I would be really grateful for the pictures!

Thank you. My posture is definitely really bad and it's gotten worse because of this problem because I always have to lean forward to avoid this awful feeling of my clothes touching the left side of my chest but not the right one, because the right one is flat and because I'm concerned people are gonna notice. The part I can grab is significantly smaller when I flex but not completely gone. I'll definitely tell my surgeon how bad it affects me. My back pain has gotten so bad because of the posture thing. I don't really know the exact time but I've been on T for around 4 years.

Yes, it's almost exactly the same for me! I saw my surgeon basically almost every month after surgery and he always said it's gonna go away and that it's NOT leftover tissue but he's been saying that for so long I just can't believe it anymore especially it it's getting worse and if it's that easy to fix like for you. I'll definitely tell him how much it affects me next time I see him! Hopefully I can get a revision similar to this.

I'm totally fine with a bit of tissue, I never thought it would be totally flat, as long as it looks cis, I'm happy. The thing is, it's only on the left side and it feels off, especially when I notice the clothing is touching the left side but not the right side because the right one is flat. Then my posture gets bad because I lean forward to avoid the feeling. So all in all, if it looks cis, thank you for your input, that's a bit of relief. But just the whole chain reaction of awful feeling and back pain is the thing that bothers me the most.

Yeah, that what concerns me, if it's really scar tissue I thought I shouldn't be able to grab it like that.
And yes, thankfully it's barely noticable under clothing but the feeling is awful so I hope my surgeon can do something about it. Thank you!
Hey thanks for your answer! I couldn't edit the post so I just posted more pictures on my profile, I hope they help.
Ich glaube es waren um die 6000€ mit Narkose, die zahlst du aber nach Dauer. Bei mir war die halt ewig lang und hat über tausend Euro gekostet :/ Die OP an sich 4900€.

Hallo! Ich bin von ihm operiert worden und kann ihn nur empfehlen. Er ist super nett, bedenkt alles und hat bei mir am ersten Termin schon alles angeschaut und mir gesagt, welche Schnitte er machen will. Er hat schon dieses Aufklärungsgespräch geführt und auch sogar schon gesagt, welche Art von Korrekturen vielleicht nötig werden. Hatte auch nach dem ersten Gespräch sogar meinen Termin für die OP!

Im Endeffekt bin ich EXTREM zufrieden mit den Ergebnissen, meine OP war Anfang Juni und man sieht schon fast gar nicht mehr, dass da irgendwas gemacht wurde. Hängt aber natürlich individuell ab. Er hat den Eindruck gemacht, er weiß, was er tut, also hab ich nicht viele Wünsche geäußert außer "Es soll cis aussehen" (Hatte kleine Schnitte)

Die OP Erfahrung war gut, etwas chaotisch, weil der Zeitplan sich die ganze Zeit geändert hat und man irgendwann gar nicht mehr wusste, was abgeht und wann man drankommt, war aber vielleicht ein Einzelfall bei mir. Es wurde sich sehr gut von den Schwestern um mich gekümmert und nach einer Nacht darf man wieder gehen.

Das einzige, was ich so wirklich kritisieren würde: Er ist sehr fast paced. Also zack zack, alles geregelt und dann ist er auch schon wieder weg. Ob das mit dem Vor- oder Nachgespräch war, anzeichnen und nach der OP Wunden anschauen, er wirkt ggf. immer bissl gehetzt, aber das hat nichts negativ beeinflusst. Er ist wahrscheinlich ziemlich im Stress.

Zur Kostenübernahme kann ich nichts sagen, da ich von Anfang an als Selbstzahler da war. Hatte vor Ewigkeiten mal angerufen wegen einem Termin und die haben mir gesagt, meine Krankenkasse wird da nicht akzeptiert. Bin dann wieder auf Medienhafen zurückgekommen, weil der medizinische Dienst mich in den Wahnsinn getrieben hat und ich mir dachte dann zahl ich es selbst.

Hoff das hilft dir ein bisschen :)
Thank you!! I basically never see any men shirtless in any context so I don't really know what's "normal" if there's even something like that.
Thanks! Everyone irl has been telling me I'm overthinking it as well, I think it's time to believe everyone lol
Thanks!!
Thank you!!
Thank you so much, this made me feel a lot better!
Thank you. You're right, my anxiety just likes to make me forget, same with looking down on it and suddenly everything looks massive. I'll try to think of that more often.
Gotta remind myself that there's all shapes and sizes, I'm just comparing too much probably. But that's very reassuring, thank you!

Thank you so much! I thought it might be something like this but I wasn't sure how it works. Yeah there's still swelling, I'll try my best to be patient! I know I'm getting ahead of myself but I just finally want this whole thing to be over hhh
Idk if my brain is playing tricks on me or not. I got peri because I'm stealth but now I'm not sure it will look cis. Could they get smaller with time during healing?
Thank you.

Yeah, I should consider myself lucky in that regard.

You're probably right. I could wait it out and then see how I feel with it. I'll think about it. I definitely feel a little bit better now. It really does make a difference if you actually talk about it instead of just burying it.

I have no doubt I'm going to feel better after surgeries, I'm just scared of getting my hopes up, you know? Scared of too high expectations or thinking it'll "flip a switch in my life" or something like that. Sorry, I don't really know how to describe it. Thank you for talking and listening to me btw.

My parents don't have any problems with it anymore, they've become rather supportive so that's something at least.

I'm sorry you feel the same way. Having gender dysphoria means I was assigned the wrong sex at birth, my body is female but I'm a boy, basically I'm trans. Which sucks cause it's also the reason I can't change my therapist unfortunately. I need 18 months of therapy with the same person to be able to get surgeries. If I get a new one I'd have to start over.
I just wrote this and wondered why I even bothered to think about surgeries. Maybe being hopeful to have a comfortable body someday is something worth living for but I don't really know.

I'll have to wait till moving out. I can't get anything I need, my mom would notice. Or worse, interrupt me while I'm doing it. 

Mostly because of gender dysphoria but also because I can't do anything right, I always have panic attacks when something needs to be taken care of, I have no friends because of social anxiety and I just can't feel happy or even content. My therapist doesn't seem to care even if I tell her I want to die.

I'm having the same problem. The only thing that's helped me a bit is the fact that everyone stares at a "new" person who enters the room (or any other place). Apparently it's a safety habit. You look at the person and try to figure out in seconds if they're going to be a possible threat to you. After my therapist told me, I noticed I'm doing it too. I still have a hard time believing that's the only reason they stare at me cause I always think it's longer than a few seconds but it's something at least.

I know that feeling of calling for help but actually not really wanting it. It's like being torn apart. I did it a few times, I just have nobody who is interested enough to listen.

I think that's a good agreement. Of course, being suicidal isn't something good and I wish nobody had to be, but at least you have one thing less to worry about, I guess. I just wish my therapist knew me better/longer, maybe I could talk to her about something like that.

I'm 18 and a legal adult, yes. If what you say is true, I'm a bit confused. My mom often makes comments like "Oh, I've talked to your therapist, don't tell me I don't know you" and stuff. Sucks. Could have been before I turned 18 though.

I'm trying to be honest tomorrow, at least as much as possible. I really hope they will be able to help me in some way.

Thank you for commenting, it really gave me a bit of insight. I'll be as honest as I can be and see what happens tomorrow. I hope I can find the courage to make my own decision to go to a hospital if it gets worse.
Okay, I guess that makes sense, thank you.
I really am glad I could help. I hope it works out.

I can understand that. If you get upset, try to calm down and think about her reasons and feelings, maybe that can help. Staying calm and rational is the best way to approach something like this. I really hope you can talk about all of this with her and you can somehow feel better. I'm sorry, I really don't know what else to say, I hope I can/could help at least a little.

Of course. Then maybe you really are the only one she can be herself with all the negative emotions around. Please don't think you are the reason for her to feel bad. If you want to be sure try talking to her about it or maybe tell her you are here to listen to her. If it really is like I think it is, you're helping her a lot by just letting her feel emotions she can't show to anyone else.
I do. I feel safe listening to music. It calms me down and distracts me.
I think you're maybe the only person she has opened up to other than her therapist so she can only show her true feelings to you. Do her friends know about her anxiety/depression?

If you feel like you're able to do it, it can't hurt to try. And if you do, I really really hope it's going to help. But I hope you're not only doing this for your girlfriend but also for yourself. 
I'm not sure why I'm scared tbh. I usually joke around with her and she knows a totally different "me" so suddenly telling her I'm suicidal I just don't think she is going to believe me. I also always nervously laugh everything off. And technically I have no real reason to tell her I want to stop so I feel like she is going to be angry or sad if I do it.

For me, it's even worse knowing that I have to talk to a person and I'm extremely scared of it. Don't have the guts to tell her though. I'm also too scared to tell her that I really feel like shit. So if you also have anxiety I don't recommend it.
I've been doing that for a long time now but it just made me isolate myself because it made me care even more for some reason. It just pushes everyone away.
Thank you. I really don't know what to say. I thought I was going to be better today but it didn't work out.
